_comment: Per-repo required status-check contexts, layered onto each repo's `main`
branch ruleset by `fleet-apply.sh --require-checks`. Origin: lentago/.github#27
(rulesets had no required checks, so `gh pr merge --auto` could not arm and a
red plan/lint blocked nothing).
Contexts are the EXACT GitHub check-run names, captured from live PR check
runs — NOT workflow names or job display names. Note the surprises: the
reusable ShellCheck check reports as 'shellcheck / shellcheck' (caller-job /
reusable-job), and kalmia's ansible-lint reports as 'ansible-lint' (the job
id), not 'Ansible Lint' (the workflow name).
HARD RULE: never list a context whose workflow is path-filtered at the `on:`
level — a required check whose workflow never triggers is held 'Expected'
forever and deadlocks every non-matching PR. The terraform repos solve this
with an always-on `gate` job (see each repo's terraform.yml). Only list
checks that report on EVERY PR (or that skip at the job level, which counts
as passing). See fleet-ops/README.md § Required status checks.
As of 2026-07-25 every active repo is mapped — there are no intentional
exceptions left. The fleet-wide adoption of the shared `docs-check` reusable
(lentago/.github#57, shared-workflows#28) is what closed the last four:
`brasenia`, `reference-checker` and `repo-template` had only advisory claude
workflows, and `shared-workflows` had nothing at all that ran on its own PRs
because every workflow there is a `workflow_call` reusable. It now dogfoods
docs-check against its own markdown via a local path ref.
`.github` gates on its own `validate` (ci/validate.py — fleet-ops config shape,
brand-asset reproducibility, census classifier routing, incident-register
reproducibility) plus the shared ShellCheck over fleet-apply.sh. Its relative-
link check was removed in #67 and replaced by the shared docs-check, so the
fleet has one link resolver rather than two drifting copies.
NOTE (2026-07-25): --require-checks REPLACES the required_status_checks rule
wholesale with what is listed here — it does not merge with what is already
live. Any context required live but absent from this file is therefore dropped
on the next sweep. That happened to site-icecreamtofightwith-com: its ruleset
required 'Lint content' + 'Compile and commit' while this file listed only the
former, so the docs-check sweep silently removed 'Compile and commit'. Restored
here. Before adding a repo, diff this file against the live ruleset — this file
is the source of truth, so anything missing from it is a deletion.
Enforced surfaces (apply-on-merge) must require their terraform `gate`:
claytonia, kalmia, drosera and solidago all do as of 2026-07-25 (.github#28).
claytonia was the last — its terraform.yml was `on:`-level path-filtered, so
requiring `terraform / validate` as originally proposed would have deadlocked
every non-terraform PR. claytonia#69 moved the filter into a `changes` detector
job and added the always-on `gate` fan-in, matching the other three.
